llm_response.content:
EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Strategy: Difference-in-Differences with an event-time (dynamic) specification.

Why it fits
•  Staggered, plausibly quasi-random program roll-out (dependent on donor arrival) yields variation across schools and over time.  
•  Panel data (1993-94 through 2004-05) permit pre- and post- comparisons within schools and contemporaneous comparisons across schools.  
•  Outcomes (AP course-taking, exam-taking, SAT/ACT, college matriculation) are measured annually at the school level.  
•  An event-study version allows us to (i) test the parallel-trend assumption graphically, (ii) gauge dynamics, (iii) detect fade-out or delayed effects, and (iv) examine pre-treatment leads for anticipation.  

Recent DID literature warns about two-way fixed effects (TWFE) with staggered timing; therefore I will estimate:  
a)  Sun & Abraham (2021) “interaction-weighted” DID, and  
b)  Callaway & Sant’Anna (2021) group-time ATT, both available in the fixest and did packages.  
Robust standard errors will be clustered at the school level, with a secondary check clustering at district level.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Treatment variable
•  Treat_it = 1 for school i in year t if the Advanced Placement Incentive Program is operating at that school in that academic year; 0 otherwise.

Treatment timing / event date
•  Event time τ = year t – year first implemented_i.  
•  τ = –1 is the omitted pre-period.

Control groups
Primary counterfactual:  
•  Schools that never adopt during sample window (≈1,380 schools).

Secondary (preferred) counterfactual:  
•  “Pipeline” schools chosen to adopt by 2008 but not yet treated by 2005 (18 schools). They have revealed willingness but no donor yet, thus closer on unobservables.

I will estimate specifications separately with (i) all never-treated schools and (ii) pipeline-only controls, then pool the two with treatment-probability weights.

No running variable/cutoff is needed; this is not an RDD.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A1.  Parallel trends: In the absence of APIP, treated and control schools would have evolved similarly on outcomes.  
     •  Plausibility: Program targeted low-income minority schools, but we can flexibly control for time-varying covariates (percent FRL, minority share, urbanicity, grade-level enrollment, district fixed effects) and inspect pre-trends in an event study.

A2.  Exogeneity of adoption timing: Conditional on school and year effects and observables, the exact year a willing school receives a donor is idiosyncratic.  
     •  Plausibility: Donor matching process is described as “scarce and idiosyncratic.” We will validate by showing no systematic relation between pre-period outcome levels/trends and implementation year.

A3.  Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers across schools):   
     •  Plausibility: Financial incentives and training are school-specific; geographic diffusion is limited. We will check by excluding nearest-neighbor schools and re-estimating.

A4.  No differential measurement error: AEIS and THECB data are administrative. Errors are unlikely to correlate with treatment.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
T1.  Selection on upward trend (early adopters were already improving).  
     •  Event-study pre-treatment leads; placebo checks using outcomes that should not react (e.g., 9th-grade enrollment).  
     •  Include school-specific linear trends as robustness.  
     •  Propensity-score re-weighting to re-balance observables.

T2.  Heterogeneous treatment effects biasing TWFE estimates.  
     •  Use SA (2021) and CS (2021) estimators instead of classic TWFE.  
     •  Report ATT(g,t) for each cohort g at times t.

T3.  Anticipation / initiative gearing up before donor arrival.  
     •  Examine τ = –3, –2 leads; drop schools showing significant pre-trends; run “donor-application year” placebo if application year ≠ adoption year is observed.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. R CODE OUTLINE
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# 0. Packages ---------------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)  # fast data handling
library(fixest)      # high-performance FE & SA estimator
library(did)         # Callaway-Sant'Anna
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load Data --------------------------------------------------------------
aeis   <- fread("aeis_1994_2005.csv")          # demographics & SAT/ACT
apdata <- fread("ap_course_exam_2000_2005.csv")
college<- fread("college_matric_2001_2005.csv")
treat  <- fread("apip_implementation.csv")     # school_id, first_treat_year

# 2. Merge & Construct Panel -----------------------------------------------
panel <- aeis %>% 
  full_join(apdata,   by = c("school_id","year")) %>% 
  full_join(college,  by = c("school_id","year")) %>% 
  left_join(treat,    by = "school_id") %>% 
  mutate(treated      = ifelse(year >= first_treat_year & !is.na(first_treat_year),1,0),
         ever_treated = ifelse(!is.na(first_treat_year),1,0),
         rel_year     = ifelse(ever_treated==1, year - first_treat_year, NA))

# 3. Main Outcome Variables -------------------------------------------------
panel <- panel %>%
  mutate(ap_exam_per100 = 100*ap_exams_taken/enrollment_grade_11_12,
         ap_pass_per100 = 100*ap_pass_scores/enrollment_grade_11_12,
         sat1100_pct    = sat1100_num / graduates,
         act24_pct      = act24_num / graduates,
         college_pct    = college_fall_enroll / graduates)

# 4. Two-way FE (baseline, aware of limitations) ----------------------------
est_baseline <- feols(ap_exam_per100 ~ treated | school_id + year, 
                      data = panel, cluster = ~school_id)
summary(est_baseline)

# 5. Sun & Abraham Event-Study ---------------------------------------------
# Create event dummies
es_data <- panel %>% 
  filter(rel_year >= -5 & rel_year <= 5) %>%   # window
  mutate(rel_year  = factor(rel_year))
sa_model <- feols(ap_exam_per100 ~ i(rel_year, ref = -1) | school_id + year,
                  data = es_data, cluster = ~school_id)
iplot(sa_model)                                 # event-study plot

# 6. Callaway & Sant’Anna Group-Time ATT ------------------------------------
did_cs <- att_gt(yname  = "ap_exam_per100",
                 tname  = "year",
                 idname = "school_id",
                 gname  = "first_treat_year",
                 data   = panel,
                 control_group = "never_treated",
                 se     = TRUE, clustervars = "school_id")
agg_simple <- aggte(did_cs, type = "simple")
summary(agg_simple)

# 7. Robustness: Drop urban schools -----------------------------------------
robust <- feols(ap_exam_per100 ~ treated | school_id + year,
                data = filter(panel, urban == 0),
                cluster = ~school_id)
etable(est_baseline, robust)

```

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6. EXPECTED RESULTS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Economic intuition: Large immediate cash incentives + reduced fees lower both financial and motivational barriers. Teacher incentives and training improve supply of AP courses.

Priors (per school-year, relative to baseline):
•  AP exams taken per 100 11th/12th graders: +8 to +12 (≈ 0.25–0.35 SD).  
•  AP passing scores per 100: +3 to +5.  
•  SAT/ACT high-score share: +1 pp (out of ~8 pp baseline).  
•  College matriculation: +2 pp.  
Potential negative spillovers on non-AP course grades or ACT participation are expected to be small (<0.5 pp).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
(C1–C5 wording follows Abadie 2023 generic checklist for DID)

C1: No interference between units (SUTVA)…………………………………… 0.8  
C2: Parallel pre-treatment trends………………………………………………… 0.7  
C3: Treatment timing as-good-as-random conditional on FE………… 0.6  
C4: No anticipatory behavior………………………………………………………… 0.7  
C5: Correct functional form / estimator handles heterogeneity……… 0.8  

Average score: 0.72 → Reasonably credible but not bullet-proof.
